findings.issue_text: Fallback chain is only pre-loaded in the web request cycle via set_locale; mailers, background jobs, and I18n.t(key, locale:) lookups never load the fallback chain, so keys missing in the target locale render as 'translation missing: xx.key' instead of falling back to English/site-default text (and I18n.t(key, locale: :fr) can return site-default text even when a :fr translation exists)

Fallbacks are now unconditionally enabled in development/test via the initializer (previously only enabled in production configs), so missing translations silently render English/site-default text instead of the 'translation missing' marker, hiding untranslated keys from developers and masking locale gaps in specs

FallbackLocaleList#[] recomputes the fallback chain (including re-reading SiteSetting.default_locale) on every backend translation lookup with no memoization, adding avoidable allocations and a setting read to the I18n hot path, especially for interpolated translations that bypass the accelerator cache

String/Symbol mismatch in the fallback chain (locale.to_s mixed with SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym and :en) defeats uniq, leaving duplicate locales in the chain and causing redundant backend lookups plus extra MissingTranslationData raise/rescue cycles for keys missing in the primary locale

I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called unconditionally in set_locale on every request, and on cold start the first request per distinct user locale per process synchronously warms up to 3 locales in the request path, potentially causing a latency spike after each deploy/restart depending on load_locale's first-load cost

goldens.comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fallback chain is only pre-loaded in the web request cycle via set_locale; mailers, background jobs, and I18n.t(key, locale:) lookups never load the fallback chain, so keys missing in the target locale render as 'translation missing: xx.key' instead of falling back to English/site-default text (and I18n.t(key, locale: :fr) can return site-default text even when a :fr translation exists)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a custom fallback chain (config/initializers/i18n.rb sets I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new) and adds a preloading hook via FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!, but the only callsite added is in ApplicationController#set_locale (I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!). Nothing in the diff triggers this for non-controller contexts (mailers/background jobs) or for I18n.t(..., locale: ...) usage. Given the TranslateAccelerator pattern shown (it only auto-loads config.locale in translate when no args/options are passed), missing preloading can plausibly cause fallbacks to resolve using only already-loaded locales, yielding "translation missing" or returning site-default/:en even when the target locale has translations but was never loaded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fallbacks are now unconditionally enabled in development/test via the initializer (previously only enabled in production configs), so missing translations silently render English/site-default text instead of the 'translation missing' marker, hiding untranslated keys from developers and masking locale gaps in specs

adjudication.rationale: The new global initializer `config/initializers/i18n.rb` unconditionally `require`s `i18n/backend/fallbacks`, mixes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` into the backend, and sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, which will run in all environments (including development/test). Previously, fallbacks were only explicitly enabled via `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` in environment-specific production/profile config files (now removed). This makes the finding about fallbacks being enabled outside production diff-verifiable; whether masking missing translations is desirable is an environment/UX/testing concern rather than a clear runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList#[] recomputes the fallback chain (including re-reading SiteSetting.default_locale) on every backend translation lookup with no memoization, adding avoidable allocations and a setting read to the I18n hot path, especially for interpolated translations that bypass the accelerator cache

adjudication.rationale: In config/initializers/i18n.rb, FallbackLocaleList#[] builds a new array and calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, uniq, and compact every time it is invoked, with no memoization/caching. Since I18n::Backend::Fallbacks will consult I18n.fallbacks[locale] during translation lookups, this puts extra allocations and a settings read on the translation path. The diff also shows interpolated translations bypass the accelerator cache (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb: translate calls translate_no_cache when args.length > 0), making the concern diff-grounded but performance-focused rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called unconditionally in set_locale on every request, and on cold start the first request per distinct user locale per process synchronously warms up to 3 locales in the request path, potentially causing a latency spike after each deploy/restart depending on load_locale's first-load cost

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call in `ApplicationController#set_locale` (runs per request). The new `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` iterates `self[I18n.locale]` which returns `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`, and calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!(l)` for each, so on a cold process and first hit of a given locale it can synchronously load up to 3 locales in the request path. `TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded!` memoizes `@loaded_locales`, so it’s only once per locale per process, but the first-request latency spike concern is still diff-grounded. This is a performance/architecture issue, not a correctness defect.
